items.one_liner: Attackers are actively exploiting the four-bug Plex2Shell chain (CVE-2026-96652 through CVE-2026-96656) to install cryptocurrency miners and proxies.
items.summary: Security researchers have confirmed active exploitation of a four-bug vulnerability chain known as Plex2Shell against exposed Plex Media Server deployments. The exploit combines server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-96652), internal function access (CVE-2026-96654), arbitrary file write (CVE-2026-96655), and unsigned codec loading abuse (CVE-2026-96656) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Honeypot observations recorded attackers from IP addresses such as 45.194.92[.]222 downloading payloads, deploying an XMRig cryptocurrency miner, and setting up proxy software. Plex previously issued security advisories urging administrators to update to version 1.43.3 or higher, noting that NAS and Docker deployments require careful verification.

Vulnerable versions: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10828
Malware deployed: XMRig cryptocurrency miner, proxy software
items.bottom_line: Administrators must update Plex Media Server to version 1.43.3 immediately to block unauthenticated Plex2Shell exploitation leading to cryptominer and proxy malware deployment.

items.title: AOS-Bench: Can LLM Agents Manage Dynamic Workloads?
items.one_liner: AOS-Bench evaluates LLM coding agents on managing concurrent dynamic workloads, revealing major efficiency gaps in stream execution.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced AOS-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based coding agents as dynamic workload managers rather than isolated task handlers. In real-world environments, coding agents must handle concurrent verification streams under shared CPU and memory limits. Testing across five model-harness pairs revealed that isolated task success does not correlate uniformly with stream success, with systems losing 13 to 23 points on heavy workloads and exhibiting wide performance dispersion on medium workloads. Execution-policy analysis showed that serial dispatch leaves 73% of heavy-workload tasks unclaimed, while a fixed concurrency of two approaches the performance of more elaborate management policies. The findings establish workload management as a distinct capability requiring specialized evaluation beyond single-task benchmarks.

Serial dispatch unclaimed tasks: 73% of heavy-workload tasks
Median CPU usage: below 30% under every policy
items.bottom_line: Developers deploying autonomous coding agents must account for workload management capabilities, as isolated task success fails to predict multi-task efficiency under resource constraints.
